UMCG Groningen | Radiology Department | 10 Feb 2025
Study: Multiparametric MRI Prostate
Reason for scan: Re-evaluation after previous prostate cancer diagnosis. Presenting PSA level: 2.4 ng/mL.
Observations: The gland measures 36.21 mL overall. Mild symmetric hypertrophy is noted, accompanied by a prominent median lobe. At the mid-gland level within the right peripheral zone, a discrete focus spans roughly 8 by 6 mm. T2-weighted sequences display intermediate signal here, matched by restricted diffusion on high b-value DWI and correspondingly low ADC values. Post-contrast dynamic imaging captures early, focal enhancement. There is no evidence of extraprostatic spread, seminal vesicle invasion, or suspicious pelvic lymphadenopathy. Neurovascular bundles remain anatomically preserved.
Conclusion:
PI-RADS 3 lesion in the right mid peripheral zone. Prostate volume 36.21 mL, PSA density 0.066 ng/mL/mL. csPCa predicted probability 0.76987416.

previous_notes.author: Dr. M. Jansen (GP)
previous_notes.text: 23 Aug 2023 - Dr. M. Jansen (GP): A review was conducted after the first biopsy confirmed ISUP Grade Group 1 disease. Following a PSA increase to 1.1 ng/mL in February 2023, the patient was directed to the urology outpatient clinic for structured re-evaluation. Mild lower urinary tract symptoms persist, currently managed conservatively with tamsulosin. Routine blood work remains stable, and the patient continues his statin regimen for hypercholesterolaemia.

previous_notes.author: Dr. M. Jansen (GP)
previous_notes.text: 19 Feb 2024 - Dr. M. Jansen (GP): Follow-up documentation recorded a PSA rise to 1.9 ng/mL compared to the prior year. Systemic complaints are absent, though mild LUTS align with his established BPH. He maintains a daily cycling commute and shares a home with his spouse and adult child. A routine gastroenterology surveillance colonoscopy concluded without abnormalities.
